title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: device health reporting dashboard (Worldwide)
summary: The dashboard description, access roles, licensing and roadmap details are supported. Hold the advice that a DeviceInfo query will find devices silent for more than 30 days: the sources do not establish that recovery route, and advanced hunting has retention qualifications. The per-device portal path also stops before selecting a device.

claims.quote: Endpoint DLP extends the activity detection and protection capabilities of DLP to sensitive items that are physically stored on Windows 10, Windows 11, and macOS (Catalina 10.15 and higher) devices.

claims.quote: The device health reporting dashboard in Microsoft Purview gives compliance and security administrators a centralized view of device readiness for Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (Endpoint DLP).

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout

claims.quote: The dashboard helps you find devices that might not be ready to receive or enforce Endpoint DLP policies because of configuration, connectivity, or version issues.

claims.claim: Learn says consolidating device health insights reduces manual troubleshooting across pages.

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" is an Advanced hunting query in Microsoft Defender portal that reads Endpoint DLP device data.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Defender portal ... Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting ... Sample query:
DeviceInfo
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, final bullet
claims.claim: A DeviceInfo query can find a device silent for more than 30 days as an alternative to the dashboard.
claims.quote: Searched: DeviceInfo advanced hunting data older than 30 days retention inactive devices Purview Devices; DeviceInfo inactive 30. Read DeviceInfo, sync and advanced-hunting-overview. No passage guarantees retrieval of such devices; hunting retention depends on the tenant and data.
claims.fix: Remove 'or a DeviceInfo query' from the final Change & support bullet. Neither cited device-data page establishes recovery of devices silent beyond the dashboard window; https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-xdr/advanced-hunting-overview qualifies the available hunting history by retention and supported data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support, final bullet
claims.claim: The Devices list can show devices silent beyond the dashboard's 30-day window.
claims.quote: To view these details, go to Device onboarding > Devices. ... Onboarded devices will continue to appear for 180 days after the device is offline.
claims.fix: After removing the unsupported DeviceInfo alternative, replace the bullet with 'A device silent for more than 30 days falls outside the dashboard data window. Check the Devices list: Microsoft's onboarding overview says onboarded devices continue to appear for 180 days after going offline.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/device-onboarding-overview#check-device-status in sources.
